newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares leap at start of New Year.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares leap at start of New Year.

text.p: Russian share prices leapt in a hectic market on the first trading day of the new year and are set to rise further although many shares recoiled from their early highs, dealers said on Sunday.
But bond yields rose at a Treasury bill auction because of a shortage of cash after the New Year holiday break.
"Expectations on the (share) market are optimistic, and a continuation of the rise can be expected," said Anton Kudryashov, head of equity trading at Renaissance Capital.

Andrei Kukk, chief trader at Rinaco-Plus, agreed the rise would continue for a few days, but said profit-taking could then hit some stocks. But demand could spread to shares which have so far not benefited from the rise, he added.

The Russian Trading System's 24-share index closed at 213.38, a rise of 6.42 percent on the 200.50 where it closed on December 31, the last trading day before the New Year break. Sunday was a working day in Russia after the four-day holiday.
Oil company Surgutneftegaz attracted the biggest interest because of plans to issue American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) this month.
ADRs allow foreign investors to buy shares while avoiding domestic settlement problems. Shares of Russian companies which have issued ADRs have often outperformed the rest of the market.
Surgutneftegaz's financial consultant Konvest said that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission had given the final approval to Surgutneftegaz's ADR issue, which would start after January 10.

Surgutneftegaz, the main operating company in Russia's third biggest oil group, finished at $0.501, up from $0.430 on December 30. It fluctuated widely during the day, hitting $0.570 at midday. Russian shares are usually traded in dollars.
Surgutneftegaz has also said it plans to issue ADRs on its preferred shares, and demand for these was strong too. They closed at $0.341 after $0.300, off an early $0.400 high.
Shares in national power company UES were also sought, rising to $0.0960 from $0.0915.
The government sold an 8.5 percent stake in UES last month, and results of the auction are due around January 17. Dealers said the price was rising in the run-up to publication of the results.
But in the government securities market, reopening for the first time since December 29, an auction of 7.50 trillion roubles of 227-day bills was under-subscribed.
The average annual yield on the paper was 36.94 percent up from 32.59 percent at the last auction, of 210-day paper, on December 25.
But it was also well above the 34.61 percent yield on the bills with the closest maturity to the new paper.

"The maturity was long, and there was little money so dealers tended to be speculative and succeeded in getting a premium to the market of four-five percent. We haven't seen something like that for a long time," said Denis Nechayev of Bank MFK.

But dealers said yields would come down at the next auction on January 8, as foreign investors buy paper to lock in the guaranteed dollar yield for non-residents, which is set to fall to 12.5 from 13.0 percent on January 16.

Sunday was also the first trading day this year for the rouble, which is in a new official trading range or corridor, running from 5,500-6,100 per dollar at the start of the year to 5,750-6,350 at the end of 1997.
But the currency market was virtually dead, with banks quoting the rouble at around 5,590 per dollar.
